body:
> Observed while running a `claude` worker on a real board. Every command shape below was denied in one attempt; the worker spent roughly 40% of its Bash calls rewriting commands to get past the allowlist, and never completed its task inside `max_runtime`.

## Why

`decidePermission` and the launched harness enforce **two different policies**, and the stricter one wins.

`src/model.js:608` declares a set of shell builtins hkb considers safe for a worker:

```js
export const SAFE_BUILTINS = ['cd', 'pwd', 'true', 'false', 'echo', 'printf', 'test', '[',
                              'env', 'which', 'command', 'type', 'sleep', 'time', 'set', 'export'];
```

`allowedCommandsFrom` (`src/model.js:618`) seeds hkb's own PreToolUse allow-set with it, so **hkb's guard permits `cd`, `export`, `which`, `test`, `sleep`.**

But `src/board.js:11-12` builds the harness allowlist from `SHELL_TOOLS` alone:

```js
const SHELL_TOOLS  = ['hkb *', 'git *', 'gh pr *', …, 'jq *'];   // no builtins
const CLAUDE_TOOLS = [...SHELL_TOOLS.map((c) => `Bash(${c})`), 'Bash(true)', 'Edit', 'Write', 'Read', 'Glob', 'Grep'];
```

`CLAUDE_TOOLS` becomes `--allowedTools`, and the profile launches `--permission-mode dontAsk`, which **denies rather than prompts**. `SAFE_BUILTINS` is never added, so the harness refuses precisely the commands hkb's own policy declares safe. `Bash(true)` is spliced in by hand — evidence the omission is an oversight, not a decision, since `true` is itself in `SAFE_BUILTINS`.

## Observed denials

All returned `Permission to use Bash has been denied because Claude Code is running in don't ask mode`. Shapes generalised; each is a real denial from one worker session:

```bash
cd <dir> && ls -la <dir>                              # cd      — in SAFE_BUILTINS
VAR="value" npm ci --no-audit --no-fund               # VAR=    — firstWords skips `w.includes('=')`
export VAR="value"; npm ci --no-audit                 # export  — in SAFE_BUILTINS
which <bin>; readlink -f "$(which <bin>)"             # which   — in SAFE_BUILTINS
while true; do hkb heartbeat <n>; sleep 300; done     # while   — a keyword, in neither list
```

hkb's own guard would have allowed the first four.

## Impact

- **Workers burn turns and budget fighting the allowlist.** Roughly 40% of one session's Bash calls were denied; it exhausted its runtime without finishing.
- **It silently breaks the heartbeat.** The fourth shape above is a worker setting up its own `hkb heartbeat` loop, exactly as `SKILL.md` asks ("run `hkb heartbeat <n>` roughly every 10 minutes"). Denied, so `heartbeat_at` never advanced from `started_at` and the task drifted toward `stale_after` while genuinely alive. A reviewer reading the run record sees a worker that never heartbeated and concludes it hung.
- **`cd` is the most common shell idiom there is.** Its absence makes multi-directory work in a monorepo needlessly awkward, and every worker rediscovers the constraint by trial and error.

## What

1. **Add `SAFE_BUILTINS` to `CLAUDE_TOOLS`** so the two layers agree:
   ```js
   const CLAUDE_TOOLS = [...SHELL_TOOLS.map((c) => `Bash(${c})`),
                         ...SAFE_BUILTINS.map((c) => `Bash(${c})`),
                         'Edit', 'Write', 'Read', 'Glob', 'Grep'];
   ```
   `Bash(true)` then falls out of the spread and the hand-splice goes.
2. **Do the same for `COPILOT_TOOLS`**, which is derived from `SHELL_TOOLS` and has the same gap.
3. **Decide on shell keywords** (`while`, `for`, `if`, `case`). They are not commands and no allowlist entry can name them; either document that workers should avoid loops in a single `Bash` call, or note in `SKILL.md` that the heartbeat is a per-turn call rather than a background loop.
4. Consider a `doctor` check that flags a profile whose `allowed_tools` omits `SAFE_BUILTINS`, since existing boards carry the generated list verbatim and will not pick up a default change.

## Done when

- [ ] A worker can run `cd`, `export`, `which`, `test` and a `VAR=value` prefix without a denial.
- [ ] The heartbeat idiom `SKILL.md` recommends actually runs under `dontAsk`.
- [ ] `COPILOT_TOOLS` covers the same set.
- [ ] `node --test test/` passes, with a case asserting `CLAUDE_TOOLS` is a superset of `SAFE_BUILTINS`.
- [ ] Existing boards get a migration path — a `doctor` warning, or a note in the release notes.
goal: A worker can run cd, export, which, test and VAR=value prefixes without a denial; CLAUDE_TOOLS and COPILOT_TOOLS are supersets of SAFE_BUILTINS; a test asserts it and existing boards get a migration path.
title: CLAUDE_TOOLS omits SAFE_BUILTINS, so dontAsk denies the commands hkb's own guard allows
